top_news.title: On-Device Named-Entity Recognition: A Deployability Study of Accuracy, Cost, Reliability, and Confidence
top_news.dek: A new study evaluates nine NER systems across three paradigms to determine real-world deployability for on-device applications.
top_news.brief: Researchers tested models ranging from 13M to 8B parameters, including spaCy, GLiNER, and generative LLMs like Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1. The study focuses on practical deployment metrics—accuracy, cost, reliability, and confidence calibration—rather than leaderboard performance, providing a framework for evaluating NER systems without human-annotated data.
top_news.image_alt: Chart comparing NER model performance and latency

top_news.title: A Flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
top_news.dek: A recently patched vulnerability in the ChatGPT macOS application could have allowed unauthorized access to sensitive user data.
top_news.brief: The flaw highlights the growing security surface area of AI-native desktop applications. While the industry often focuses on the risks of AI agents, this incident serves as a reminder that the software wrappers themselves are critical targets for exploitation.

top_news.title: DeepSeek Harness Desktop for macOS and Windows
top_news.dek: DeepSeek has launched an open-source desktop client for macOS and Windows to interface with its models.
top_news.brief: The DeepSeek Harness desktop app is now in public preview, supporting everyday tasks and coding workflows. The project is open-source and features a plugin architecture, allowing developers to extend functionality. It is available for download on Apple Silicon and 64-bit Windows.

top_news.title: Sidecars: A low-latency trust boundary for Sandboxes
top_news.dek: Modal introduces Sidecars to provide a low-latency, secure trust boundary for sandboxed execution environments.
top_news.brief: Sidecars run as isolated containers alongside the main sandbox on the same host. This architecture addresses the challenge of protecting users from their own code, offering a more modern security approach than traditional isolation methods like gVisor or Firecracker for agentic workflows.

top_news.title: AWS Strands Labs Releases Strands Decider 2B: An Open Source Decision Model That Picks Options in About 115 ms
top_news.dek: AWS Strands Labs released Decider 2B, an open-source model optimized for rapid decision-making and routing.
top_news.brief: Built on Qwen3.5-2B-Base, Decider 2B outputs choices and confidence scores in a single forward pass without generating text. It achieves a 115ms median latency on an RTX 3090, making it suitable for real-time agent guardrails, tool selection, and routing tasks.

primary.summary: AWS's Strands Agents team released Strands Decider 2B, an Apache-2.0 decision model built on Qwen3.5-2B-Base. It returns choices, yes/no probabilities and scores with calibrated confidence in one forward pass, never text. It runs at a 115 ms median on an RTX 3090 and scores 0.723 on the JevBench public set, which makes it a fast local option for routing, tool selection and guardrails in AI agents.
